items.title: Argentina Is Ramping Up Its Claim to the Falklands. Here’s What to Know.
items.author: Qasim Nauman
items.content: <article>President Javier Milei has dialed up Argentina’s claim over the British territory, while President Trump has raised questions about longstanding U.S. neutrality on the dispute.</article>

items.title: Judge Ends Federal Oversight of Teamsters
items.author: Rebecca Davis O’Brien
items.content: <article>The union and federal prosecutors agreed that organized crime groups had been rooted out of union operations, the judge wrote.</article>

items.title: Former Labor Secretary Stoked Dysfunction and Toxicity, Department Report Finds
items.author: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Lydia DePillis
items.content: <article>Lori Chavez-DeRemer spent Labor Department funds on personal travel and tolerated harassment in the agency, its inspector general found.</article>

items.title: Trump Taps Army Engineering Official as Acting Secretary
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>The move came days after the resignation of Daniel P. Driscoll, who had clashed with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the purge of top generals in the Army.</article>

items.title: Trump to Break Ground on Arch Before Getting Approval
items.author: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
items.content: <article>Doug Burgum, the interior secretary, announced plans to start work on the site of the 250-foot-tall triumphal arch. Final approval of the project is still pending.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Limits
items.author: Abbie VanSickle
items.content: <article>The justices have been asked to weigh in again on the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict mail voting — this time on whether the plans violate the Constitution.</article>

items.title: Judge Suggests Trump Mail-In Voting Rules Could Cause ‘Major Disenfranchisement’
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>Judge Indira Talwani said the Postal Service appeared to be trying a haphazard “experiment” with a new rule that could result in valid ballots being tossed.</article>

items.title: Proposal for White House Visitor Screening Center Advances
items.author: Aishvarya Kavi
items.content: <article>A federal panel again paved the way for one of President Trump’s construction projects, even as it heard opposition to another proposal to fence in a park north of the White House.</article>

items.title: JD Vance Says He Wouldn’t Call Iran Conflict a War
items.author: Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>In the first White House press briefing since Karoline Leavitt left as press secretary, the vice president suggested that when the conflict would end was up to Tehran.</article>

items.title: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and Others Pay Tribute to Gloria Steinem
items.author: Johnny Diaz
items.content: <article>After Ms. Steinem’s death at 92, celebrities and politicians reflected on her decades of activism for women’s rights and equality.</article>

items.title: Gloria Steinem, Personification of the Feminist Movement, Dies at 92
items.author: Katharine Q. Seelye
items.content: <article>She challenged sexist assumptions, helping women develop a sense of self-worth and gain a measure of equality at work, at home and in society at large.</article>

items.title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
items.author: Colby Smith
items.content: <article>Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.</article>

items.title: Trump’s D.C. Makeover Projects Are ‘Only an Idea,’ Until They’re Much More
items.author: Emily Badger
items.content: <article>A proposed garden of heroes is following a familiar path in which facts on the ground move faster than the courts and others can keep up.</article>

items.title: Is Letting Only Seniors Vote by Mail Unconstitutional?
items.author: Adam Liptak
items.content: <article>Federal appeals courts have split on the question, making Supreme Court review likely.</article>

items.title: El-Sayed Wants to Mend Ties With Jewish Democrats, but Some Are Still Not Impressed
items.author: Bayliss Wagner and Steve Friess
items.content: <article>Lingering concerns about the Senate nominee in Michigan could make it harder for him to assemble a winning coalition.</article>

items.title: Homeland Security Secretary’s Plane Makes Emergency Landing
items.author: Karoun Demirjian
items.content: <article>The landing was the latest close call over Washington’s congested airspace to involve a senior government official.</article>

items.title: White House Plans $250,000 Renovation of 2-Lane Bowling Alley
items.author: Mack Liederman
items.content: <article>A White House spokesman said the alley renovations included fixing broken lights. The project comes as the president has sought a broad overhaul of the White House and its surroundings.</article>

items.title: Judge Blocks Trump’s Second Try to Restrict Birthright Citizenship
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>The ruling raised concerns that babies already defined as citizens by the Supreme Court could have their citizenship revoked under an order the president signed in August.</article>

items.title: As Midterms Loom, Democrats Feud Over Defections
items.author: Michael Gold
items.content: <article>The fight has highlighted party divisions and raised questions about how Democrats will run the House should they win the majority.</article>

items.title: In the Midterms, Will the Nepo-Baby Attack Work?
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>A New Hampshire senator’s daughter is running for office, and finds her name being used against her.</article>
